scholarshipName: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master scholarship — ReSound (EMJM Sound Design for Media Arts)
provider: European Commission / EACEA, via ReSound consortium (FilmEU alliance)
whoCanApply: Open to non-EU nationals incl. Tunisians. Official page: "ReSound is open to both European and non-European students who hold a bachelor's degree in sound, music, film, or media studies." Applicants from other fields may qualify with relevant prior experience. YES — a Tunisian is eligible (Partner Country / non-EU scholarship category).
ageLimit: No age limit stated on the application page — EMJM has no age cap. He clears it.
subjectScope: Sound design, sound production, composition and execution across media arts — film, TV, games, immersive media, VR. Directly on-target.
coverage: EMJM scholarship: 1,400 EUR/month living allowance; no tuition fees for scholarship holders (self-funded fee is EUR 15,000 total). EMJM standard also includes contribution to travel/installation and insurance. Exact travel/installation figures for this consortium: UNVERIFIED.
numberOfAwards: "A maximum of 24 places are offered ... each year" (places, not all scholarship-funded); exact number of EMJM scholarships per intake: UNVERIFIED
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE: "Applications for ReSound 2026 have now closed." Expected 2027-cycle window: call opens autumn 2026 (Oct–Nov 2026), deadline typically Jan–Feb 2027 for a Sept 2027 start. EXACT 2027 DATE UNVERIFIED — monitor resound-ma.eu from Oct 2026.
howToApply: Apply directly to the consortium via resound-ma.eu/application/ — one application covers admission and the EMJM scholarship. Not via a single university.
requiresAdmissionFirst: No — the consortium application IS the scholarship application; admission and scholarship are decided together.
languageRequirement: English. "IELTS 6.0 (all components >=6.0) or equivalents like TOEFL iBT 79, Duolingo 110, or Cambridge B2, taken within two years." His working English is likely sufficient but he must sit a test.
competitiveness: UNVERIFIED (EMJM programmes typically 10–30 applicants per funded place)
notes: HIGHEST-VALUE TARGET. Portfolio required: "Please supply no more than 3 examples" of sound/media work with reflective paragraphs, 10–15 minutes of material. His BSc is not in sound/music/film/media, so he must lean on the "relevant prior experience" clause — the portfolio is what makes or breaks him. Start building it now.

scholarshipName: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master scholarship — DIGICREA (Digital Creativity, Art & Science)
provider: European Commission / EACEA, via DIGICREA consortium (Université Jean Monnet Saint-Étienne, Universidade Católica Portuguesa Porto, University of Silesia Katowice/Cieszyn)
whoCanApply: "open to artists and creators worldwide, including both students and professionals (minimum requirement: a bachelor's degree)" — a Tunisian is eligible. Non-EU applicants fall in the EMJM Partner Country scholarship bracket.
subjectScope: Audiovisual new media, emerging technologies in film, MUSIC, graphic design, AI, VR. Music is explicitly named. Open to a computing/engineering bachelor.
coverage: EUR 1,400/month for 24 months; EMJM standard tuition waiver plus travel/installation contribution (exact figures for this consortium UNVERIFIED)
numberOfAwards: "up to 17 students per cohort" receive the scholarship
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE: 15 February 2025 (midnight French time), extended to 20 March 2025, interviews March 2025. Expected 2027-cycle window: deadline circa Jan–Mar 2027. EXACT 2027 DATE UNVERIFIED.
applicationOpens: Typically Nov–Dec of the preceding year (UNVERIFIED for 2027)
howToApply: Directly to the consortium via https://master-digicrea.univ-st-etienne.fr — single application for admission + scholarship; interview stage.
languageRequirement: English (French useful in Saint-Étienne). Exact test thresholds UNVERIFIED.
notes: One of the very best fits for a software engineer moving into art/sound: art+science framing rewards his coding background. His French fluency is a real advantage for the Saint-Étienne semester. Interview stage — prepare a project pitch.

scholarshipName: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters — general scheme (all catalogue programmes)
whoCanApply: Any nationality worldwide, including Tunisia (Tunisia is a Partner Country / 'not-Programme country'). Students apply to individual consortia; scholarships are reserved partly for non-EU applicants.
ageLimit: No age limit anywhere in the EMJM rules. He clears it.
subjectScope: All disciplines — catalogue of 100+ programmes. Music/sound/media/digital-creativity entries exist (ReSound, DIGICREA, Resono, plus media/film/heritage programmes).
coverage: Full tuition waiver + EUR 1,400/month living allowance + contribution to travel and installation costs + insurance. (Commission: "covers tuition fees, travel expenses, installation costs, and a monthly living allowance of EUR 1,400".)
numberOfAwards: Typically ~15–25 scholarships per programme per intake, across 100+ programmes
deadline: Varies per consortium; the vast majority fall between November and February for the following September start. For a Sept-2027 start: deadlines Nov 2026 – Mar 2027.
applicationOpens: Most consortia open October–November 2026 for the 2027 intake. 37 NEW EMJM projects were selected on 16 July 2026 and are expected to enter the catalogue and open applications in autumn 2026 for a Sept-2027 start — check the catalogue again in Oct 2026 for new sound/media entries.
howToApply: Directly to each consortium (not to the Commission, not to a single university). Apply to several in parallel — there is no central cap.
competitiveness: UNVERIFIED per programme; Commission does not publish per-place ratios
notes: THIS IS HIS SINGLE BIGGEST OPPORTUNITY CLASS. No age cap, no requirement for a music degree at most consortia, fully funded, and Tunisians are in the favoured non-EU bracket. Apply to 4–6 in the same cycle. Official catalogue: https://www.eacea.ec.europa.eu/scholarships/erasmus-mundus-catalogue_en

scholarshipName: DAAD Study Scholarship — Master Studies for All Academic Disciplines
whoCanApply: Graduates from a listed set of countries. Tunisia's inclusion for this specific programme: UNVERIFIED — the page says "Your status and/or country is not in the list? If your status and/or country is not included in the list, you cannot apply for this scholarship programme." He must select Tunisia in the country filter on the DAAD database to confirm. DAAD does run scholarship activity in Tunisia (DAAD Information Centre Tunis), so it is likely eligible.
ageLimit: No explicit age limit, but a RECENCY cap: "As a rule, your most recent university degree should not date back more than 6 years at the time of the application deadline." Graduating now, he clears this comfortably for a 2027 start.
subjectScope: All academic disciplines. NOTE: artistic fields (music, fine art, performing arts, architecture) are handled by SEPARATE DAAD programmes — a music-production/electroacoustic master at a Musikhochschule may be pushed to the artistic scheme, which he cannot use (see below). A music-TECHNOLOGY / audio-engineering / media-informatics master at a regular university fits this all-disciplines scheme.
coverage: 992 EUR/month; annual study allowance of EUR 460; payments toward health, accident and personal liability insurance; travel allowance on application; possible rent subsidy. DAAD explicitly does NOT cover tuition fees (most German public universities charge none).
deadline: Applications open 1 June each year. For funding beginning in 2027 (scholarship usually starts 1 October 2027), the deadline is reported as 31 August 2026 — i.e. ALREADY IMMINENT. VERIFY on the DAAD portal immediately; deadlines vary by country and are updated annually.
howToApply: Online via the DAAD portal (portal.daad.de). He applies to DAAD directly.
requiresAdmissionFirst: Not at application time, but admission is required before the funding period begins: he must "ensure their application for admission to the German university for your chosen study programme is submitted by the due date".
languageRequirement: Proof of proficiency in the language of instruction; certificate no older than 3 years. German or English depending on programme.
notes: FLAG: DEADLINE MAY BE 31 AUGUST 2026 — that is roughly 13 months before the September 2027 start and is within weeks of today (12 Aug 2026). This is the most urgent item in this whole list. Check the DAAD database with country=Tunisia TODAY.

scholarshipName: DAAD Study Scholarship — Postgraduate Studies in the Field of Music
whoCanApply: "The programme is aimed at graduates from the field of Music" and requires "a first degree in music by the time the scholarship begins". HE IS NOT ELIGIBLE — he has no music degree. Tunisia's presence on the country list is separately UNVERIFIED.
ageLimit: No age cap; recency rule: "As a rule, your university degree should not date back more than 6 years at the time of the application deadline."
subjectScope: Artistic music only: "This programme only funds projects in the artistic field. Other DAAD scholarship programmes are available for applicants from the field of musicology or music education."
coverage: 992 EUR/month, one-off study allowance, health/accident/liability insurance, travel allowance and possible rent subsidy on application
deadline: Varies annually; applications possible between 1 June and the stated deadline. EXACT 2027-cycle deadline UNVERIFIED.
requiresAdmissionFirst: No, but: "A scholarship award does not automatically mean admission to one of the colleges of music... If an applicant positively selected by DAAD is not admitted to any university, the scholarship already awarded cannot be used."
languageRequirement: Sufficient knowledge of the language of instruction by scholarship start
notes: LISTED SO HE DOES NOT WASTE TIME ON IT. The music-degree prerequisite rules him out unless he first obtains a music qualification. Route to Germany is the all-disciplines scheme plus a music-technology/audio programme at a technical university (e.g. TU Berlin Audio Communication, Detmold/Paderborn Musikinformatik).

provider: Campus France / French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs
whoCanApply: Non-French nationals; Tunisians are eligible in principle. BUT applications are institution-nominated: "Only applications submitted by French higher education institutions are accepted."
ageLimit: "applicants from foreign countries up to 29 years old at master's level" — at 24–26 he CLEARS this comfortably.
subjectScope: PROBABLE BLOCKER. Two priority fields only: Sciences & technology (biology and health, ecological transition, mathematics and digital technology, engineering sciences) and Human & social sciences (history, French language and civilisation, law and political science, economics and management). ARTS AND MUSIC ARE NOT LISTED — a music-production or electroacoustic-composition master is very likely ineligible. UNVERIFIED whether a music-technology master could be squeezed under 'mathematics and digital technology' / 'engineering sciences'.
coverage: Master's: EUR 1,200/month (from January 2026), plus economy return airfare (reimbursed up to 50% of the ministry's maximum rate), health insurance enrolment via Campus France, supplementary cover free, CROUS or private housing placement, cultural activities. Does NOT cover tuition at private schools.
duration: Master's: up to 12 months (24 for entry at M1, 36 for engineering)
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE (2026 session): call opened 1 October 2025; Campus France deadline 8 January 2026; results from 30 March 2026. Expected 2027-cycle window: call opens circa 1 October 2026, deadline circa early January 2027.
howToApply: VIA THE FRENCH INSTITUTION, not by the student. He must be admitted/shortlisted by a French public institution and ask its international office to nominate him internally — internal institutional deadlines typically fall in NOVEMBER, two months before the Campus France deadline.
requiresAdmissionFirst: Effectively YES — he needs a French institution willing to put his file forward, which in practice means an application/admission process running Oct–Nov 2026.
languageRequirement: Programme-dependent; his French fluency is a strong asset.
notes: FLAG: the internal institutional nomination deadline is around November 2026 — about 10 months before the Sept-2027 start. Only public institutions delivering a national diploma qualify (so conservatoires delivering a DNSPM/master and public universities, not private audio schools). Subject scope is the main risk — verify against the 'Eiffel Programme rules – 2027 Session' PDF when published.

whoCanApply: Citizens of Chevening-eligible countries — Tunisia IS eligible (dedicated country page: chevening.org/scholarship/tunisia/). BUT: "You must have at least 2800 hours of work experience, acquired after the completion of your undergraduate degree" and "If you completed your undergraduate degree after October 2024, you cannot apply." HE IS NOT ELIGIBLE for the 2027/28 cycle — he is graduating in 2026 with no professional experience.
ageLimit: "there is no upper age limit" — no age barrier; the work-experience rule is the barrier.
subjectScope: Any one-year taught master's at a UK university, including arts/music/creative courses. Subject is not restricted.
coverage: Full tuition, monthly living stipend, return economy airfare, arrival/departure allowances, visa and IHS costs, thesis grant, homeward journey. Exact 2027 amounts: UNVERIFIED.
duration: One year (one-year UK taught master's only)
deadline: CONFIRMED: 6 October 2026, 11:00 UTC for the 2027-2028 cycle. *** THIS IS ELEVEN MONTHS BEFORE THE SEPTEMBER 2027 START — the classic trap. ***
applicationOpens: Already open (announced as open as of August 2026)
howToApply: Directly to Chevening online (chevening.org). Three UK course choices are named in the application; unconditional offer from one is needed by mid-July of the start year.
requiresAdmissionFirst: No at application; yes later — an unconditional UK offer is required by a July deadline in the start year.
languageRequirement: Chevening English language requirement (met via a UK offer/test). Exact level UNVERIFIED.
competitiveness: UNVERIFIED (globally reported as roughly 3–4% success, but not officially published per country)
notes: *** FLAG: DEADLINE 6 OCTOBER 2026 — 11 MONTHS BEFORE START. *** He CANNOT use it in 2026. He becomes eligible only once he has 2,800 post-bachelor work hours (~2 years FTE), i.e. realistically the 2029/2030 cycle. Note: internships and VOLUNTARY work count toward the 2,800 hours — if he starts logging paid/unpaid studio, sound, or engineering work now, he shortens the wait.

scholarshipName: Türkiye Bursları — Arts Scholarship Programme (Sanat Bursu)
provider: YTB — Presidency for Turks Abroad and Related Communities, Republic of Türkiye
whoCanApply: "Citizens of all countries" — Tunisians eligible; Türkiye Bursları is heavily used by North African/Arab applicants. Arts programme targets performing arts, music and fine arts at Ankara Music and Fine Arts University, Ankara Hacı Bayram Veli University and İstanbul Technical University (ITU has the well-known MIAM centre for advanced music studies).
ageLimit: "being under the age of 30" for master's applicants (measured as of 1 January of the application year). At 24–26 he CLEARS it comfortably.
subjectScope: Performing arts, music and fine arts. ITU MIAM offers Sonic Arts / Music Technologies master's — direct fit for electronic music.
coverage: Full tuition, monthly stipend, accommodation, health insurance, return flights, one year of Turkish language course. Exact 2027 stipend amount in TL: UNVERIFIED (master's level stipend is set annually by YTB).
duration: 2 years master's + 1 year Turkish language preparation (3 years total funding)
deadline: Arts Scholarship Programme applications are received "between 10 January and 20 February" each year. For a Sept-2027 start: circa 10 January – 20 February 2027. EXACT 2027 DATES UNVERIFIED until YTB publishes the calendar.
howToApply: Directly via the Türkiye Scholarships Application System (TBBS) at turkiyeburslari.gov.tr. Single free application; he ranks up to 12 programme preferences. Includes an interview stage at the Turkish embassy/consulate.
requiresAdmissionFirst: No — YTB places successful candidates into a programme; he does not apply to universities separately.
languageRequirement: None at application for English-taught programmes; Turkish preparation year provided. Portfolio/audition may be required for the arts track (UNVERIFIED).
competitiveness: UNVERIFIED (YTB has reported >150,000 applicants for ~5,000 places across all levels — roughly 3% overall)
notes: One of very few fully-funded government schemes that has an explicit ARTS/MUSIC track AND accepts a non-music bachelor's. ITU MIAM (Center for Advanced Studies in Music) in Istanbul teaches sonic arts and music technology in English. Strong realistic option. Also check the general (non-arts) programme for music-technology degrees at ITU.

provider: Tempus Public Foundation / Hungarian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade
whoCanApply: Tunisia is a partner country with a dedicated country page (stipendiumhungaricum.hu/country/tunisia/). Sending partner is the Tunisian Ministère de l'Enseignement Supérieur, which nominates candidates. "applicants are eligible to apply only for those scholarship types and study fields that are determined in the educational cooperation programmes in effect between Hungary and the specific Sending Partner" — so the Tunisian bilateral agreement may restrict fields. UNVERIFIED whether music/arts is inside Tunisia's field list.
ageLimit: No age limit in the general call. He clears it.
subjectScope: All fields in principle; Hungary's Liszt Ferenc Academy of Music and Moholy-Nagy University of Art and Design (MOME) participate. Whether Tunisia's bilateral quota covers arts fields: UNVERIFIED — reported open fields for Tunisia are Engineering, Medicine, IT, Business.
coverage: Full tuition waiver; monthly stipend (HUF 43,700/month for master's level — VERIFY current figure in the 2027 call); free or subsidised accommodation or a housing contribution (HUF 40,000/month); medical insurance. Amounts UNVERIFIED for the 2027 call. Does NOT cover flights.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE (2026/27): 15 January 2026. Expected 2027/28: application period opens November 2026 with a deadline circa 15 January 2027. UNVERIFIED.
howToApply: TWO-STEP: online at apply.stipendiumhungaricum.hu AND a parallel application to the Tunisian Sending Partner (Ministry of Higher Education), which nominates. He must satisfy both.
requiresAdmissionFirst: No — the application is a combined admission + scholarship application; he ranks up to 2 study programmes.
languageRequirement: Per programme; English-taught programmes usually B2. Portfolio/entrance exam for arts programmes.
notes: The Tunisian Ministry nomination step is the bottleneck and its internal deadline can be EARLIER than the Hungarian one. Contact the Direction Générale de la Coopération Internationale at the Ministère de l'Enseignement Supérieur (Tunis) in autumn 2026. Weak on music unless the bilateral field list is broadened.

scholarshipName: Banach NAWA Scholarship Programme (Stefan Banach Programme)
provider: NAWA — Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange, funded by Polish Aid
whoCanApply: Citizens of 36 Polish Aid countries. TUNISIA IS ELIGIBLE — listed in Group 3 for the 2026/27 edition. For second-cycle (master's) full-time studies at universities supervised by the Polish Minister of Science and Higher Education.
ageLimit: No age limit stated. UNVERIFIED but the call has historically had none. He clears it.
subjectScope: CAUTION — the Banach programme has historically restricted fields to engineering/technical, agricultural and exact/natural sciences (with some social sciences for certain groups). Whether ARTS/MUSIC is eligible is UNVERIFIED and probably NOT. His software-engineering background could be used for a music-technology/sound-engineering degree in a technical faculty (e.g. AGH Kraków Acoustic Engineering, Gdańsk Tech Sound Engineering) — that route is much more likely to qualify.
coverage: Monthly scholarship PLN 2,500; exemption from tuition fees at public universities; NAWA-funded Polish preparatory course (Polish-track); travel allowance PLN 2,500.
duration: 2 years (plus 1 preparatory year for the Polish-language track)
numberOfAwards: ~300 reported for the 2026 winter-semester edition (UNVERIFIED as official)
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE: 8 May 2026, 15:00 CEST, "or until the application limit in a specific group is reached". Expected 2027 cycle: circa March–May 2027. UNVERIFIED.
howToApply: Directly in the NAWA IT system: https://programs.nawa.gov.pl/login
requiresAdmissionFirst: No — NAWA places selected candidates; he indicates programme preferences.
languageRequirement: Polish or English track; English track requires a certificate (level UNVERIFIED).
competitiveness: First-come/first-served element ("or until the application limit in a specific group is reached") — apply EARLY on opening day.
notes: Read the annual call PDF (nawa.gov.pl/images/Banach/...) for the exact field list before investing time — the field restriction is the make-or-break. Gdańsk University of Technology's Sound Engineering and AGH's Acoustic Engineering are the natural targets for his profile.

scholarshipName: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarship — ARTS Scholarship (ESKAS)
provider: Swiss Confederation, State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation (SBFI/SERI), Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students (FCS)
whoCanApply: "Art scholarships are open to students wishing to pursue an initial Master's degree in an artistic field in Switzerland." Available "to students from a limited number of countries only". TUNISIA'S INCLUSION IN THE ARTS LIST IS UNVERIFIED — the 2027-28 country-specific list is published from August 2026 on sbfi.admin.ch. Tunisia has historically been on the Swiss research-scholarship list; the arts list is shorter. CHECK IMMEDIATELY (list due this month).
ageLimit: "The maximum age is 35" for the arts scholarship. At 24–26 he CLEARS it.
subjectScope: Artistic fields — an initial master's at a Swiss university of the arts (e.g. Zürcher Hochschule der Künste, Haute école de musique de Genève, HEMU Lausanne, HKB Bern). ZHdK and HEM Geneva both run electroacoustic / sound-arts / music-technology masters. Directly relevant.
coverage: Monthly stipend CHF 2,450. Other elements (tuition waiver, health insurance, one-off arrival allowance, housing allowance, half-fare travel card, flight) are standard in the ESKAS package but the 2027-28 figures are UNVERIFIED.
duration: Up to 3 years for an arts master's (UNVERIFIED for 2027-28)
deadline: Country-specific. "Applications open August 20, 2026" and "Information on application deadlines and scholarship available by country of origin will be published here in August 2026." Deadlines usually fall between September and December 2026 for a September 2027 start.
howToApply: "Applications are submitted to Swiss diplomatic representations" — i.e. the Swiss Embassy in Tunis. Paper/portal application to the embassy, not to the university.
requiresAdmissionFirst: Arts track normally requires prior contact with, and often a pre-acceptance/audition from, the Swiss art university. VERIFY in the 2027-28 country factsheet.
languageRequirement: French, German or English depending on the school; his French fluency is a major advantage for Geneva/Lausanne.
notes: *** URGENT: applications open 20 AUGUST 2026 and country deadlines can be as early as September–November 2026, i.e. 10–12 months before the Sept-2027 start. Email sgs@sbfi.admin.ch and the Swiss Embassy in Tunis THIS WEEK to ask whether Tunisia is on the 2027-28 ARTS list. *** CHF 2,450/month is the highest monthly stipend on this entire list.

scholarshipName: Italian Government Scholarship (MAECI / 'Study in Italy' Borse di Studio) — including AFAM
provider: Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MAECI)
whoCanApply: Foreign citizens of listed countries and Italians resident abroad. TUNISIA IS AMONG THE ELIGIBLE COUNTRIES for the 2026/27 call. Applicants must not already hold an Italian degree, must not be enrolled in an Italian university, must not have had a MAECI grant in the past 5 years.
ageLimit: Age caps apply by course type (historically 28 for master's/AFAM courses, 30 for PhD, 28 for research). EXACT 2027 CAP UNVERIFIED — at 24–26 he very likely clears it, but this is one to check in the call PDF.
subjectScope: EXPLICITLY INCLUDES AFAM — "all AFAM institutions (conservatories, academies of fine arts, dance schools) are eligible". Italian conservatories run superb Musica Elettronica / Music and New Technologies biennio (2nd-level) courses (Conservatorio di Milano, Bologna, Torino, Padova, Firenze, Cagliari, Napoli). This is one of the very best subject fits available on a government scheme.
coverage: EUR 900/month for 9 months = EUR 8,100 (figures reported as EUR 10,800 for study programmes in some secondary sources — VERIFY in the official call), tuition-fee exemption where the institution grants it, and health insurance cover. Language-and-culture courses funded at EUR 3,600. Does NOT include flights.
duration: Renewable, typically 6 or 9 months per academic year, renewable for a second year on merit
numberOfAwards: UNVERIFIED (a Tunisia country quota is set annually)
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE (2026-27): 26 March 2026, 14:00 Rome time. Expected 2027-28 window: call published ~February 2027, deadline ~late March / early April 2027.
howToApply: Online only via https://studyinitaly.esteri.it — he applies to MAECI directly and names the institution/course.
requiresAdmissionFirst: No formal admission required at application, but he must have applied/pre-registered to the AFAM institution; conservatories require an entrance exam and portfolio.
languageRequirement: Italian B2 for Italian-taught courses (most conservatory biennio courses are in Italian) — or English for English-taught degrees. THIS IS HIS MAIN OBSTACLE IN ITALY: he would need to reach Italian B2. As an Arabic/French speaker Italian is comparatively fast to learn.
notes: Best subject-match of any national government scheme, because AFAM conservatories are explicitly funded. Pair this with a regional DSU/right-to-study grant (see separate entry) which can stack on top and is means-tested rather than merit-tested.

scholarshipName: Italian Regional Right-to-Study Grants (DSU / borsa di studio regionale — e.g. DSU Toscana, ERGO, EDISU Piemonte, ADiSU, Lazio DiSCo, ER-GO Emilia-Romagna)
provider: Italian regional right-to-study agencies (funded by regions + national FIS)
whoCanApply: Any enrolled student, including non-EU internationals, who meets INCOME and MERIT thresholds. Nationality is irrelevant — a Tunisian IS eligible. He must produce a certified statement of family income and assets from Tunisia, legalised by the Italian consulate in Tunis (or via the Tunisian authorities), which is the practical hurdle.
ageLimit: Usually none, but some regions cap the number of years of eligibility. UNVERIFIED per region.
subjectScope: Any field, INCLUDING conservatories/AFAM — DSU agencies cover AFAM students in most regions. Covers music-technology biennio students.
coverage: Typically EUR 5,000–7,500/year cash for out-of-region/international students, PLUS free university accommodation OR a housing allowance, PLUS free canteen meals, PLUS full tuition-fee exemption. This is often larger in real terms than the MAECI grant. Exact amounts vary by region and year — UNVERIFIED.
duration: Renewable annually for the standard course duration (2 years for a biennio)
numberOfAwards: Legally an entitlement for all who meet the thresholds in most regions (Tuscany, Emilia-Romagna, Piemonte are 100% coverage regions); some southern regions run out of funds.
deadline: Typically late August / early September of the enrolment year (e.g. DSU Toscana ~early September). For a Sept-2027 start: circa August–September 2027. UNVERIFIED per region.
howToApply: Directly to the regional agency's portal after (or while) enrolling. Separate from the university application.
requiresAdmissionFirst: Effectively yes — he applies as an incoming/enrolling student.
competitiveness: Not competitive where funding is guaranteed — it is threshold-based, and a Tunisian family income will almost certainly fall well under the ISEE-parificato threshold.
notes: THE MOST UNDER-USED MONEY ON THIS LIST for a candidate from a lower-income country. Combined with a tuition-free public conservatory this can amount to full funding without winning any competitive award. Requires an 'ISEE parificato' produced by an Italian CAF from Tunisian income documents — start that paperwork months early.
